name: Flashscore
tagline: Live scores, fixtures, tables and results across dozens of sports, updated in near real time.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. The core product is free and ad-supported, so there may be no meaningful subscription to replace.

verdictSummary: The interface is trivial: a list of matches, a score, a minute counter, some tables. Everything that makes Flashscore useful sits upstream of the interface, in licensed low-latency data feeds covering thirty-odd sports and thousands of competitions down to regional third divisions. Free sports APIs exist, but they cover a handful of big leagues, rate-limit you hard, and lag the actual match by minutes, which is exactly the gap that matters when the whole point is knowing now. You can absolutely build a personal scoreboard for the four competitions you care about, and it will be fine, and it will also quietly be a worse Flashscore. Since the product is free anyway, the trade is polling limits and coverage holes in exchange for no ads.
coreLoopDIY: A local dashboard that polls a free football API for a handful of competitions you follow and shows today's fixtures, live scores and standings on one auto-refreshing page.
requirements: A free football-data.org API token in .env
Node 20+ and a machine that can stay awake to poll
Acceptance that coverage is football only, and only the leagues the free tier includes
whatYouLose: Sub-minute updates. Free tiers are delayed and rate-limited, so your 'live' score is a guess with a timestamp
Breadth: tennis, basketball, hockey, esports, plus the long tail of lower divisions and cup qualifiers
Twenty years of archived results, head to head records and per-player stats
Push notifications on a phone you actually carry
Lineups, live commentary, cards, substitutions, xG and the rest of the match-detail layer
moatNotes: The real asset is a network of data collection deals and in-venue scouts feeding a pipeline that has to be fast at global scale, plus the archive nobody else bothered to keep.
whyPeopleStillPay: Most people do not pay, they pay in ads, and they keep coming back because the thing is instant, exhaustive and works on a decade-old phone on hotel wifi. Nothing you build reaches the obscure league you actually care about, and nothing you build updates a goal within seconds of it happening. The ad-free rivals in this space compete on the same feeds, not on the frontend, which tells you where the value sits.
notes: The scoreboard is an afternoon; the feed behind it is not. The moat is licensed real-time data collection across thousands of competitions, plus the archive of results nobody else kept.
prompt:
Build a personal live football dashboard called Scoreboard. Single Node 20 + TypeScript project, no framework beyond Fastify, server-rendered HTML, no React, no build step beyond tsc.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Fastify serving HTML strings, plain CSS in one file, zero client JS except a meta refresh every 60 seconds
- SQLite via better-sqlite3 for caching API responses
- Data source: football-data.org v4 REST API, token read from process.env.FOOTBALL_DATA_TOKEN
- .env with FOOTBALL_DATA_TOKEN and COMPETITIONS (comma separated competition codes, default PL,BL1,SA,PD,CL)

What it does:
- On startup and then every 60 seconds, fetch today's matches for the configured competitions and upsert them into SQLite
- Fetch standings for each competition at most once per hour and cache them
- GET / renders three sections: LIVE (matches in play, with score and minute), TODAY (scheduled, kickoff in local time), FINISHED (final scores)
- GET /table/:code renders the cached standings for one competition
- Serve stale cache and show a small 'last updated' line if the API call fails; never crash on a 429

Hard rules:
- Respect the free tier rate limit: a single shared request queue, max 10 requests per minute, exponential backoff on 429
- No accounts, no telemetry, no external CSS or fonts, no Docker
- README states plainly that free-tier data is delayed by minutes and covers only major competitions

Out of scope: push notifications, other sports, odds, lineups, historical archives, xG, anything resembling a mobile app.

Deliver: npm install, npm run dev, works on http://localhost:3000, plus a seed script that populates the cache once so the page is not empty on first load.
